findings.heading: Daily individual tracking / Suivi quotidien individuel
findings.proposition: The recommended visualisation for per-contact daily follow-up status is a heat plot; the French says it is a scatter plot ("diagramme de dispersion").
findings.reader_consequence: A French reader is told the chunk below builds a scatter plot, while `geom_tile()` builds a heat plot. The reader learns the wrong name for the technique and cannot connect it to the linked heat-plot page, nor reach for `geom_tile()` when a heat plot is wanted.

findings.heading: Transmission Matrices / Matrices de transmission
findings.proposition: The chunk that follows creates a heat map of age-by-age transmission; the French says it creates a geographic map ("une carte géographique pour l'âge").
findings.reader_consequence: A French reader expects a map of places from a chunk that plots age classes on both axes with `geom_tile()`. The reader misreads the whole transmission-matrix example and may look for absent geographic columns.

findings.heading: Data cleaning / Nettoyage de données
findings.proposition: The follow-up status values in the data are `seen_not_ok` and `seen_ok`; the French names them "vu_not_ok" and "vu_ok", which appear nowhere in the data or the code.
findings.reader_consequence: The `tabyl(followup_status)` output right below prints `seen_ok` and `seen_not_ok`. A French reader cannot match the explained values to the printed table, and any filter written from the prose (`followup_status == "vu_ok"`) returns zero rows.

findings.heading: Plot over time / Graphe dans le temps
findings.proposition: The column assigned to the x-axis is `date_of_followup`; the French names it `date_du_suivi`, a column that does not exist in the `followups_clean` data frame.
findings.reader_consequence: A French reader copying the prose writes `aes(x = date_du_suivi)` and gets an object-not-found error, while the chunk two lines below uses `date_of_followup`.

findings.heading: Demographics / Démographie
findings.proposition: The package used for age pyramids is named **apyramid**; the French names it **apyramide**.
findings.reader_consequence: A French reader tries to install or load a package called `apyramide`, which does not exist on CRAN. The `p_load()` chunk and the `apyramid::age_pyramid()` calls both use `apyramid`, so the prose and the code disagree.

findings.heading: Daily individual tracking / Suivi quotidien individuel
findings.proposition: The follow-up day number is computed as the difference between the encounter date and the intended follow-up start date; the French says it is the difference between the date of the LAST encounter ("la date de la dernière rencontre") and that start date.
findings.reader_consequence: A French reader building the missing follow-up-day column computes one value per contact from the last encounter, instead of one value per encounter row. The resulting column cannot drive the 1-14 x-axis of the heat plot below.

findings.heading: Data cleaning / Nettoyage de données
findings.proposition: Wide-format follow-up data commonly arrive as an Excel sheet; the French drops the Excel sheet entirely and says only "sous la forme d'une large".
findings.reader_consequence: A French reader loses the concrete example of the format these data usually arrive in, and the sentence is left without a noun, so the wide-versus-long point is harder to recognise in their own Excel exports.
